cited_evidence: Job 2 input evidence_sources contain record_id values s01 through s08 while needs/coverage record_id values are n06-r01 through n06-r08.

In upstream_demand_provenance.py, assemble_provenance appends {"record_id": record.get('source_id', ""), "source_id": record.get("source_id", ""), ...}, replacing the demand record identity with the source identity.

In downstream_coverage_priority.py, prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources.record_id and looks it up with coverage.record_id, so s01 cannot match n06-r01; the observed priorities therefore all have upstream_rank: 0.
The behavioural criteria require preserving record_id/source provenance and ranking unsupported needs first, then preserving upstream provenance order.
initial_receipt.explanation: The downstream output loses upstream provenance order: every priority has upstream_rank 0, so the ranking cannot actually preserve the demand-descending provenance order required by the criteria. The visible cause is upstream evidence construction: assemble_provenance emits evidence_sources with record_id set to the source_id (s01, s02, etc.) instead of the need record_id (n06-r01, n06-r02, etc.). Job 2 then receives those exact handoffs and cannot match evidence_sources.record_id against coverage record_id values, producing upstream_rank 0 for all records.
